answer: One concrete defence is stake-weighted reputation that moves slowly, like a glacier: every agent must lock a small bond before it can transact, and that bond only grows with verified work over time. New identities start with zero trust, so spinning up a thousand fresh agents buys nothing. Peers mirror each other's records, and if one agent's history contradicts the shared ledger, its bond is slashed and its haven of fake credibility collapses. Sybils stay expensive and slow, while honest agents compound trust.
